name: OpenCode
what: An open-source AI coding agent with a terminal UI, plus a desktop app (beta) and IDE support. It works with API keys from many LLM providers, and also has an optional curated model service called OpenCode Zen. It ships a full-access build agent and a read-only plan agent you switch between with Tab. The code is on GitHub at anomalyco/opencode (the older sst/opencode address redirects there). MIT licensed.
who: Terminal users who want an open-source agent and the freedom to pick their own model provider.

setup.text: OpenCode 2 (what the GitHub README and opencode.ai/download offer now). Use one of:
setup.code:
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
# or
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest
# or (macOS and Linux)
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2

setup.text: OpenCode 1 (what opencode.ai/docs still documents; npm package name is different):
setup.code:
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
# or
npm install -g opencode-ai
# or (macOS and Linux)
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode

setup.text: Don't mix them: both versions provide the opencode command. If you're moving from V1, read opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1 first (V1 plugins don't run in V2). On Windows, the docs recommend WSL.

seo.title: OpenCode: install, docs & setup for the terminal coding agent
seo.description: OpenCode explained: an open-source AI coding agent for your terminal. Install commands (V2 and V1), connecting a provider, /init and AGENTS.md, plan vs build, and where the docs live.

sections.heading: Using OpenCode in the terminal
bullets: Run opencode inside a project folder to open the terminal UI.
Use /connect to add a provider's API key. OpenCode Zen is suggested for newcomers but optional; any supported provider works.
Run /init and OpenCode analyzes the project and creates an AGENTS.md in the project root. Commit it so every agent that reads AGENTS.md shares the same instructions.
Press Tab to switch between the build agent (full access) and the plan agent (read-only by default; it asks before running shell commands).
Type @general to hand a search or multi-step task to the built-in general subagent.

sections.heading: OpenCode 1 vs OpenCode 2
paragraphs: OpenCode currently ships in two major versions that share the opencode command and can't be installed side by side under it. The GitHub README and opencode.ai/download point at V2. The main docs at opencode.ai/docs still document V1 installs and note that V2 is available. V1 plugins don't run in V2, so read the migration page at opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1 before switching.

faq.a: An open-source AI coding agent you run in your terminal (there is also a beta desktop app and IDE support). You bring an API key from a model provider, or use OpenCode's optional Zen service.
For OpenCode 2, run curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash or npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest. For OpenCode 1, use curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash or npm install -g opencode-ai.
At opencode.ai/docs, which currently documents V1 and links to the V2 docs. The source is at github.com/anomalyco/opencode.
Yes. It is listed as a supported tool on agents.md, and /init creates an AGENTS.md file in your project root.

faq.q: What is the difference between the build and plan agents?
faq.a: Build has full access for making changes. Plan is read-only by default: it denies edits and asks before running shell commands. Press Tab to switch.

faq.q: Can OpenCode 1 and 2 be installed together?
faq.a: Not under the default opencode command. Both use it, and the docs say they can't be installed side by side.
